words.desc: A person who keeps and checks financial records and prepares tax returns.
A person who pretends to be a character in films, plays or television.
A person who plans and designs buildings and oversees how they are constructed.
A person who makes paintings, drawings and other creative visual works.
A person trained to travel and work aboard a spacecraft beyond Earth.
A person who trains hard and competes in sports or physical events.
A person who makes bread, cakes and similar goods in an oven for sale.
A person who works in finance, managing money, loans and investments for clients.
A person who cuts men's hair and trims or shaves beards.
A person who heats and hammers iron to shape tools and metal objects.
A person whose job is to construct and repair houses and other structures.
A person who operates a large public vehicle that carries passengers along set routes.
A person who cuts and sells meat, usually from a shop or market counter.
A tradesperson who cuts, shapes and joins timber to build or repair things.
A person whose job is to take customers' payments in a store.

A comic performer who wears bright costumes and face paint to make people laugh.
A person who trains athletes or a sports team and plans how they play.
A person whose trade is mending and making footwear.
A performer whose job is making audiences laugh with jokes and funny stories.
A person employed to carry packages or documents quickly from one place to another.
A person who moves rhythmically to music, often as a performance.
A health professional who looks after people's teeth and gums.
A person who plans the look and function of products, graphics or spaces.
A person who investigates crimes and gathers evidence to find out who is responsible.
An official who represents their country abroad and handles relations with other nations.
A person trained to examine sick people and treat their illnesses and injuries.
A tradesperson who installs and repairs wiring, sockets and power systems.
A person who uses maths and science to design and build machines or structures.
A person who grows crops or raises animals on rural land for food.
A person trained to put out blazes and rescue people from danger.
A person who catches marine creatures from boats, rivers or the shore for a living.
A person who arranges and sells cut flowers and plants in a shop.
A person who looks after plants, lawns and flower beds for a living.
A person trained to cut, colour and style people's tresses, usually in a salon.
A person who builds a large online following and promotes products to fans.
A person who cleans and maintains a school or other large building.
A person who gathers information and writes news stories for the public.
An official who presides over a court and decides the outcome of cases.

A person who manages a collection of books and helps people find information.
A person who watches over swimmers and rescues them if they get into trouble.
An entertainer who performs tricks and illusions that seem impossible.
A person who delivers letters and parcels to homes and businesses.
The elected leader who runs a town or city.
A person who repairs and maintains vehicles and their engines.
A person paid to pose for photographs or show clothes on a runway.
A person who plays an instrument skilfully, often performing for audiences.
A person trained to look after patients and assist with their medical care.
A trained responder who gives emergency care to people before they reach hospital.
A health professional who prepares and dispenses medicines and advises on their use.
A person who takes pictures with a camera, often for a living.
A person who flies an aircraft, such as a passenger jet.
A tradesperson who installs and repairs water pipes, drains and bathroom fixtures.
A member of the force that keeps public order and enforces the law.
A person who seeks or holds an elected position in government.
A person ordained to lead religious services and perform sacred rites.
The person in charge of running a school and its staff.
A senior academic who lectures and researches at a university.
A person who writes instructions that make computers and software work.
A professional who studies the mind and helps people with emotional or behavioural difficulties.
An official who enforces the rules during a sports match.
A person who works on a ship or boat as part of its crew.
A person who studies the natural world through careful observation and experiments.
A person employed to protect a building or event and keep people safe.
A person who uses their voice to perform melodies, often professionally.
A person who serves in an army and is trained for combat.
A person who secretly gathers information about an enemy or rival.
A person who broadcasts live video of themselves online for an audience.
A medical specialist who operates on patients to repair or remove damaged tissue.
A person who makes, alters and repairs clothing to fit a customer.
A person paid to take passengers wherever they want to go in a car.
A person whose job is to help pupils learn, usually in a classroom.
A person who converts written text from one language into another.
A person whose job is to transport goods by road in a large vehicle.
A person paid to give private lessons to one pupil or a small group.
A medical professional who treats sick and injured animals.
A person who serves food and drinks to customers at their tables in a restaurant.
A person who creates books, stories or articles as their work.
A person who feeds and cares for the animals kept in a wildlife park.
